pages.text: Few creatures have Time to spare: $(l)phantoms$(), $(l)endermen$(), the $(l)undead$(), and the very young. An $(l)amethyst needle$() draws it, but ordinary glass cannot hold it: it ages to sand in my hand.$(br2)A vial lined with phantom membrane, a $(l)Stasis Ampoule$(), holds a little.

Take too much Time from one place and the place $(o)tears$(). A $(l)Time Tear$() ages everything around it and swallows anything dropped near it. Heavy things keep time still: four drams of $(l)Density$() press a tear shut.
pages.title: Time Tears

pages.text: Injecting Time into myself lets me $(l)stutter$() the world around me for a moment. It also leaves a ticking in my ears that does not stop for a long while. If the ticking turns into skipping... I will write that down when it happens.
pages.title: Self-Experimentation
